A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAA research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting a reliable comparison. All pages were checked; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4 report original forgetting analyses, model evaluations and ablations, presented in Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original forgetting analyses, Llama2 and Qwen2.5 evaluations, and grouping and sampling ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same vulnerability grouping, robust objective, curriculum and adversarial sampling updates. The alternative grouping approaches mentioned in v2 are future suggestions, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both use BeaverTails-derived alignment and harmful data, Alpaca for proxy grouping, and SST-2, AG News, GSM8K and AlpacaEval for downstream evaluation. Newly cited factuality and watermarking work introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain SFT, RepNoise, Vaccine and Booster. Tables 5–6 retain the same grouping and sampling comparators; the newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 preserves model sizes, sample counts, HS/FA metrics, full-parameter training, learning rates, batch size and epochs. The poison-ratio, epoch and cross-model evaluation settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the forgetting and loss-landscape analyses, poison-ratio and epoch robustness tests, cross-model grouping transfer, and grouping/noise and sampling ablations. v2 adds no analyses testing its proposed future directions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 mentions uncertainty estimation only as a possible future grouping approach, not as uncertainty reporting for its results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 2–3 retain the same results and findings. For example, Table 1 reports VAA's average harmful score of 24.82 and fine-tuning accuracy of 56.77 in both versions; no result entries are added.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same vulnerability and common-forgetting definitions, robust objective, GDRO formulation and sampling-update derivation. No mathematical assumptions, proofs or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and central conclusion retain the claims of uneven data vulnerability and improved safety through vulnerability-aware group optimization while preserving task performance. Combining VAA with other alignment methods was already proposed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 expands v1's brief future-work discussion into explicit limitations: simple grouping depends on pseudo fine-tuning, and VAA does not entirely prevent alignment breakdowns. It additionally suggests uncertainty/factuality-based grouping and watermarking for protection and traceability.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, four 80GB A100 GPUs, runtime and backpropagation-cost information, and the code-access link remain unchanged. The new limitation highlights an already documented pseudo fine-tuning step rather than disclosing a new procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references covering permutation robustness, uncertainty estimation, factuality and watermarking, mainly supporting the expanded future directions. The central positioning against existing HFT defenses and the claimed DRO contribution remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The conclusion receives localized rewriting and a labeled Limitations paragraph that reorganizes and expands existing future-work discussion. Other wording edits are small, and the main section structure and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with modest spacing and placement changes. Table 5 moves from the lower-left to the upper-right of page 8 above Table 6, and the acknowledgments and references reflow.

improvement.justification: The explicit limitations make the dependence on pseudo fine-tuning and the incomplete protection against alignment breakdowns clearer than v1's brief future-work discussion. This improves transparency modestly; the method and evidence remain unchanged, and the suggested alternative metrics and watermarking integrations are untested.
